title: Preamble & Recitals: Parties, Dates and Prior-Lease Background
where_to_look: The opening preamble/caption naming the instrument and identifying the parties and signatories; the WHEREAS/"Recitals" or "Background"/"Antecedentes" section immediately preceding the Definitions or first operative section; and any property/premises description or defined-term block (e.g., "Existing Lease," "Initial Lease," "the Lease") located there.
required: The Recitals/Background section must: (1) name each party's exact current legal entity and the individual signing on its behalf, with a representation that the signatory's authority (officer or attorney-in-fact) is current and has not been revoked, modified, or limited; (2) state a single, unambiguous execution/effective date that is consistent across every language version and every cross-reference to that date elsewhere in the document (signature blocks, exhibits, term-commencement language); (3) if the instrument amends, renews, or extends a pre-existing lease, recite that prior lease — and each intervening amendment — by exact title and date, and define an umbrella term (e.g., "Existing Lease") that expressly includes the base lease together with all amendments, commencement-date memoranda, and addenda that together comprise the operative lease relationship; and (4) carry forward (rather than silently drop) any representation still being relied on for signing authority or corporate capacity unless Marmon's counsel confirms it is redundant with a document that remains in force.
fallback: Accept a streamlined recitals section that drops older corporate-capacity, tax-status, and notarial boilerplate carried over from a prior instrument — this is common and generally low-risk on renewal — provided the chain-of-title essentials survive: the prior lease and any amendments are still identified by name and exact date, and the umbrella defined term ("Existing Lease"/"Initial Lease") still captures every document that is actually part of the deal (base lease, amendments, and any commencement/errata memoranda). Minor recital-format differences (WHEREAS clauses vs. numbered Antecedentes, English vs. bilingual drafting) are acceptable as long as this substance is preserved.
escalate_if: Escalate to an attorney regardless of how negotiations are going if: the recitals omit or misstate the date or identity of a prior lease/amendment that this instrument is actually amending or renewing; a representation of continuing signing authority (attorney-in-fact/officer authority) is dropped from a renewal or amendment without confirmation that the underlying authority is still valid; recitals in one language version conflict with another (e.g., different dates for the same referenced document) and are not reconciled before signature; the "Existing Lease"/"Initial Lease" defined term excludes a memorandum, amendment, or addendum that is actually part of the operative deal, risking that key terms (rent, term, premises) are not properly incorporated; or the property/premises description in the recitals conflicts with the description used in the operative sections or exhibits with no reconciling reference.
flag_if: Preamble execution/effective date does not match the date on signature blocks, exhibits, or other cross-references in the document
Operative provisions reference "as amended," "Extended Term," "the Lease," or similar language presupposing a pre-existing lease that the recitals never identify

A defined term like "Existing Lease," "Initial Lease," or "the Lease" is used before being defined, or is defined to cover only one instrument when context shows multiple related documents (base lease plus amendments/memoranda) are actually involved
Bilingual or multi-version recitals give inconsistent dates, entity names, or signatory details between language versions
Corporate-capacity, tax-status, or signing-authority representations from a prior lease are silently dropped in a renewal/amendment with no cross-reference confirming they remain valid
Party legal name or signatory in the preamble does not match the name/signatory used in the signature block or in a related guaranty or amendment
confidence_note: Based on 14 usable findings (2 additional findings were excluded as flagged document-pairing/OCR noise, not genuine negotiated redlines) across 9 distinct counterparties/deals spanning US, Mexican, Polish, and Singaporean leases — Hannibal Industries, GLG Properties (two separate matters), PDC Industrial Center Warsaw, Indiana Athletic Apparel, Pool 4 Industrial TX, Whitney Architects, Royal & Sons Investments, FAE Holdings, and Creekside SPE. The direction is fairly consistent (recitals/background sections are repeatedly added, tightened, or corrected to properly identify parties, dates, and prior-lease chains), but significance is mixed (4 high, rest medium) and this reads more as a recurring drafting-accuracy issue than an adversarial, high-stakes negotiating position — hence PRESS rather than MUST PRESS, with genuine but occasional escalation-worthy risk (e.g., a dropped attorney-in-fact authority representation, an unresolved cross-language date discrepancy) rather than a uniformly dangerous pattern.

title: Party & Guarantor Substitution (Successor-in-Interest / Corporate Restructuring)
where_to_look: Preamble/recitals (Landlord/Lessor and Tenant/Lessee identification), the Guaranty preamble (guarantor identification), the Notices section (addresses and "copy to" requirements), and any successor-in-interest, assignment, or "definition of the Lease" language in amendments/extensions.
required: Whenever Landlord, Tenant, or Guarantor has been renamed, converted to a different entity form, merged, or otherwise succeeded by another entity, the operative document must: (a) name the current, correct legal entity and its form (e.g., "formerly known as," "converted to a Delaware LLC," "successor-in-interest to"); (b) expressly recite the chain of succession/conversion so the relationship to the predecessor entity is documented on the face of the lease, not merely assumed; (c) confirm all obligations (including any guaranty) continue uninterrupted and binding on the successor without release of the predecessor absent a signed assumption/release; and (d) require that notices be copied to Marmon Holdings, Inc.'s (or the current parent's) in-house legal/real estate group in addition to notice to the local business unit.
fallback: If the counterparty will not accept full successor-in-interest recital language, secure at minimum: (i) the current correct legal name, entity form, and address for every party and guarantor: (ii) a one-line statement that the name/entity change does not affect the validity or continuity of the lease or guaranty; and (iii) retain the notice-copy-to-parent-legal-and-real-estate requirement, which has been obtainable even when fuller succession language was not.
escalate_if: Escalate to an attorney if a party's name changes in a lease document with no recital or evidence tying the new entity to the prior one (e.g., a materially different landlord entity appears with no "successor-in-interest," assignment, or deed reference); if no supporting documentation (assignment and assumption, certificate of conversion/merger, deed) is available on request; or if a guarantor is substituted without a fresh or reaffirmed guaranty executed by the new guarantor entity.
flag_if: Party name in the preamble/recitals does not match the name in the signature block or notice address, with no explanation
A landlord, tenant, or guarantor name has changed since the prior lease document but no "successor-in-interest" or "formerly known as" recital was added
Guarantor's stated entity name does not match the actual signatory's employer, or no updated/reaffirmed guaranty was executed alongside a guarantor substitution
Notice provision does not require a copy to Marmon Holdings, Inc. (or current parent) legal/real estate group

An amendment or extension purports to reference "the Lease" or prior amendments but the current and prior documents show low textual similarity, suggesting they may not actually be sequential drafts of the same agreement
Entity form changed (e.g., Corporation to LLC) but is reflected inconsistently across preamble, defined terms, signature block, and notice address
preferred_language: Successor Parties; Entity Changes. If Landlord, Tenant, or Guarantor is renamed, converts to a different form of entity, merges, consolidates, or is otherwise succeeded by another entity (whether by corporate restructuring, conversion, merger, assignment, or transfer of the underlying property or guaranty obligation), the party undergoing such change shall provide the other party written notice within thirty (30) days of the effective date, together with reasonably available documentation evidencing the change (e.g., a certificate of conversion or merger, an assignment and assumption agreement, or a deed). Any lease, amendment, guaranty, or notice executed on or after such change shall (a) identify the current legal name and entity form of the affected party, (b) expressly state that such party is the successor-in-interest to, or formerly known as, its predecessor, and (c) confirm that all obligations under this Lease and any related guaranty continue in full force and effect and are binding on the successor entity without interruption, release, or discharge of the predecessor's obligations absent a written assumption and release signed by Landlord. All notices under this Lease shall be delivered to Tenant at the address stated herein and shall also be copied to Marmon Holdings, Inc., Attention: Chief Legal Counsel - Real Estate, at its then-current notice address, or to such successor department or address as Tenant may designate in writing from time to time.
confidence_note: Based on 4 findings across 3 distinct counterparties/deals (NAVA-guarantor renaming; Providence Properties-landlord and tenant identification; 319 LLC-landlord succession and tenant entity conversion), with significance high in 3 of 4 and the direction consistent (correct current entity naming, explicit succession recitals, notice-copy-to-parent requirements) — but one finding (the Providence Properties to JEM Land landlord substitution) was itself flagged in the source data as ambiguous, since low document similarity left it unclear whether it reflects a genuine successor change or two unrelated documents, so treat this rule as directionally sound but based on a small and partly uncertain sample.

title: Order of Precedence & No-Novation (Amendment vs. Underlying Lease)
where_to_look: In the amendment/renewal/extension document itself — typically near the end, under headings like "Order of Precedence," "Entire Agreement," "No Novation," "Ratification," or folded into General/Miscellaneous Provisions. Also check the original Lease's standalone provisions (especially Attorneys' Fees, Indemnification, Guaranty, Security Deposit) to see whether they are being restated, silently dropped, or left to survive by implication only.
required: Include both an order-of-precedence clause AND a no-novation/survival clause in the same amendment: (1) the new document controls over the underlying Lease (as previously amended) only as to the specific matters it expressly addresses; (2) the underlying Lease and all prior amendments remain in full force and effect and are not extinguished, replaced, or novated by the new document; and (3) all terms not expressly modified — including attorneys'-fees/fee-shifting rights, indemnification, guaranties, and security — expressly survive and continue unchanged.
fallback: Where the counterparty resists a full ratification/survival clause, accept the narrower pairing actually observed in practice: an order-of-precedence sentence (new document controls only where inconsistent with the prior Lease/amendments) plus a no-novation confirmation naming the prior Lease and amendment(s) and confirming their continued effect — but still insist on adding an express carve-out preserving attorneys' fees, guaranties, and security so they are not silently dropped just because they aren't repeated in the new document.
escalate_if: The new document's precedence/integration language is broad enough to arguably supersede or extinguish the entire underlying Lease (not just the inconsistent provisions) — this risks unintentionally discharging guaranties, security, or fee-shifting rights, as nearly happened when a Letter Extension's precedence clause coincided with the disappearance of the original Lease's attorneys'-fees provision. Also escalate if any language could be read as effecting a novation of the Lease or an underlying guaranty (which in some governing-law jurisdictions can discharge a guarantor/surety), or if a no-novation confirmation is expressly refused where a guaranty or security instrument backs the Lease.
flag_if: A renewal/amendment/extension is being added on top of an already-amended Lease (multiple prior documents) with no order-of-precedence clause stating which document controls in a conflict.

Standalone provisions from the original Lease (attorneys' fees, indemnification, insurance, guaranty) are absent from the new document and there is no express survival/no-novation clause confirming they remain in effect.
The new document contains a broad 'entire agreement' or integration clause with no carve-out preserving the underlying Lease's terms except as expressly modified.
No-novation language is missing even though the Lease is backed by a corporate guaranty or security deposit.
Absolute supersession language such as 'this Amendment/Extension supersedes the Lease' rather than 'governs only to the extent inconsistent with the Lease as previously amended.'
preferred_language: Order of Precedence; No Novation. This [Amendment/Renewal/Extension] amends and supplements, but does not replace, novate, or discharge, the Lease dated [___] between the parties, as previously amended by [identify prior amendment(s)] (collectively, the "Lease"). Except as expressly modified by this [Amendment/Renewal/Extension], all terms, covenants, conditions, and rights of the Lease remain unchanged and in full force and effect, including without limitation any attorneys'-fees or fee-shifting provisions, indemnification obligations, guaranties, and security deposits or other security instruments given in connection with the Lease. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this [Amendment/Renewal/Extension] and the Lease, the terms of this [Amendment/Renewal/Extension] shall control, but only with respect to the specific matters expressly addressed herein. The parties expressly agree that execution of this [Amendment/Renewal/Extension] does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, a novation of the Lease or of any guaranty or security given in connection therewith, and all obligations of any guarantor thereunder shall continue in full force and effect without interruption. This [Amendment/Renewal/Extension], together with the Lease and all prior amendments thereto, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, and there are no other agreements or understandings, oral or written, not expressly referenced herein.
confidence_note: Based on only 3 findings drawn from 2 distinct counterparties/contracts (a GLG Properties lease renewal contributing 2 findings, and a 319 LLC letter extension contributing 1) — the direction is consistent (parties add order-of-precedence and no-novation protections during renewals, and the real danger is a precedence/integration clause silently dropping standalone rights like attorneys' fees), but with only two underlying deals this is a thin sample; priority is set to PRESS rather than MUST PRESS, and the rule should be revisited as more findings on this topic become available.

title: Expansion of Premises / Additional Leased Space
where_to_look: The Recitals and the "Premises"/granting-clause section of any lease amendment or addendum that adds space to an existing tenancy, and the correlated Rent, Term, Use, and Insurance sections of that same document (both findings show the expansion mechanic living in a newly added Recitals + restated "Premises"/"Expansion of Premises" operative section, with downstream edits to Term/Rent and Insurance/Use).
required: Document any addition of space to an existing Marmon tenancy as a formal written amendment (not an informal side letter or an ambiguous freestanding "new lease") that: (a) recites and expressly incorporates the original lease by date and parties; (b) precisely defines the added space (e.g., "Expansion Premises"/"Additional Premises") by exact square footage and an attached exhibit/site plan/legal description; (c) states unambiguously whether the added space merges into a single combined "Premises" defined term or is tracked as a separate space, and states the resulting total square footage; (d) sets the incremental rent (or rate) for the added space with its own clear commencement date; (e) makes the term of the added space co-terminous with the original lease term unless deliberately and expressly staggered; and (f) confirms Tenant's insurance, use rights, and other lease obligations extend to the expanded space.
fallback: Where the counterparty insists on a separate, free-standing addendum/second lease for the added space (as in the McKenzie Valve/Tommy Surber "Lease 2" addendum) rather than a full amendment to the original lease, accept it only if that addendum: expressly cross-references the original lease by date/parties, expressly states it does not disturb Tenant's rights under the original lease, and independently but fully addresses rent, term, insurance, and use for the added space with protections comparable to the primary lease.
escalate_if: Escalate to an attorney regardless of how negotiations are going if: the combined/total square footage or the boundary between original and expansion premises is left ambiguous or unstated; the term or expiration date of the added space is not addressed (risking a mismatched holdover or expiration relative to the original lease); the counterparty uses the expansion document as a vehicle to reopen or weaken unrelated terms of the original lease (e.g., renewal options, exclusive-use rights, default/remedies provisions) that have nothing to do with the space being added; or new "combined Premises" language could be read to cross-default or cross-terminate the original and expansion spaces together when the parties intended them to be severable.
flag_if: Expansion/addition of space documented only by informal correspondence or email rather than a signed amendment or addendum
New document does not reference the original lease's date and parties (unclear whether it's an amendment or an unrelated new lease)
Added space's square footage or boundaries not specifically stated, or no exhibit/site plan/legal description attached
Incremental rent or rate for the added space not clearly stated as a defined amount, or no stated commencement date for the new rent
Term/expiration of the added space not explicitly aligned with (or expressly and deliberately staggered from) the original lease term
Insurance, use, or other lease obligations not updated to reference the expanded or combined premises
"Premises" redefined as a single combined term without clarifying whether original lease rights (renewal options, ROFR, exclusive use, etc.) extend to the new space
Rent/Term changes for the expansion space are bundled into a broader 'Miscellaneous' or savings-clause section rather than clearly itemized
preferred_language: EXPANSION OF PREMISES. Landlord and Tenant may from time to time agree to add space to the Premises leased under this Lease by executing a written amendment to this Lease (each, an "Expansion Amendment"). Each Expansion Amendment shall: (a) reference this Lease by its original date and the parties hereto; (b) identify and describe the additional space (the "Expansion Premises") by square footage and by reference to an exhibit or site plan attached to the Expansion Amendment; (c) state whether the Expansion Premises is merged into and becomes part of the "Premises" as defined in this Lease or is instead added as a separately identified and tracked space, and in either case state the combined total square footage of the Premises following such addition; (d) state the incremental Base Rent (or Base Rent rate) payable for the Expansion Premises and its commencement date; (e) state the term applicable to the Expansion Premises, which shall be co-terminous with the Term of this Lease unless the Expansion Amendment expressly provides otherwise; and (f) confirm that Tenant's insurance obligations, use rights, and other obligations under this Lease extend to and cover the Expansion Premises. Except as expressly modified by an Expansion Amendment, all other terms and conditions of this Lease shall remain in full force and effect and shall apply equally to the Expansion Premises. [First draft only; not reviewed by counsel.]
confidence_note: Based on only 2 findings — a Hannibal Industries lease amendment (request 1757) and a Tommy Surber/McKenzie Valve addendum (request 3715) — both significance "high" and pointing the same direction (properly cross-referencing the original lease and separately spelling out rent/term/insurance for the added space, whether via a merged "Expansion Premises" or a separate "Lease 2"); the direction is consistent but the sample is thin (2 findings, 2 counterparties), so this rule should be treated as provisional and priority is set to PRESS rather than MUST PRESS pending more examples.

title: Permitted Use Scope
where_to_look: The "Use" / "Permitted Use" clause (often in the lease's definitions section, e.g. Section 1.01, or a standalone "Use" section such as Section 4 or 5); also check any lease amendment's renumbering/restatement of that section (e.g., where a "Use" section gets folded into a general "Miscellaneous" savings clause) to confirm the original use restriction wasn't silently narrowed or dropped.
required: A permitted-use clause that names the primary intended use(s) broadly (e.g., by general category such as "office, warehousing, manufacturing, and/or light-industrial" rather than a single narrow product/activity) AND expressly includes a catch-all for "uses ancillary, incidental, or related thereto" (including administrative, sales, storage, and distribution activities). Avoid provisions requiring Landlord's consent for any change in use; if consent is required, it should be limited to non-ancillary changes and not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
fallback: If Landlord will not agree to a broad category-based use description, fall back to a use clause that names the specific primary use(s) but still adds an express "and uses ancillary or incidental thereto" allowance (as opposed to a single, standalone, no-ancillary-use restriction). This is where negotiations have most consistently landed in practice.
escalate_if: Landlord insists on (a) a single, narrowly-defined use tied to one specific product/activity (e.g., "for [X] only") with no ancillary/incidental-use allowance, combined with (b) a requirement that Tenant obtain Landlord's prior consent (especially in Landlord's sole discretion) for any change in use or in materials/activities on the Premises. That combination creates real default/operational risk if Marmon's business needs shift and should not be accepted without attorney review.
flag_if: Permitted use is tied to one specific narrow product, process, or activity (e.g., 'Rail Car Testing/Research' or storage of one named material) with no ancillary/incidental/related-use language
Any change in use, or in the materials/goods handled at the Premises, requires Landlord's prior written consent with no reasonableness standard

An amendment renumbers or restates the 'Use' section into a generic 'Miscellaneous' or savings clause in a way that makes it unclear whether the original use restriction survives, was narrowed, or was dropped
Use clause has no express carve-out for ordinary ancillary functions (administrative, sales, storage, distribution) incident to the primary use
Use description does not match Tenant's actual or reasonably anticipated operations at the Premises
preferred_language: Permitted Use. Tenant may use the Premises for general office, warehousing, manufacturing, and/or light-industrial purposes consistent with applicable zoning classifications, together with any uses ancillary, incidental, or related thereto (including without limitation administrative, sales, storage, and distribution activities in support of Tenant's operations), and for no other purpose without Landlord's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Tenant's use of the Premises shall at all times comply with applicable zoning ordinances and legal requirements. No amendment, restatement, or renumbering of this Section shall be deemed to narrow, waive, or terminate the permitted uses described herein unless expressly and specifically stated.
confidence_note: Based on only 3 findings across 3 different counterparties (Hannibal Industries, East End Maker Hub Sponsor LLC, Indiana Athletic Apparel LLC); 2 of the 3 clearly and consistently show Marmon's side pushing to broaden a narrow, single-purpose use restriction into a broader category plus an "ancillary/related uses" allowance, but the third finding's outcome is ambiguous (unclear whether the original restriction survived an amendment's renumbering) — treat this rule as directionally sound but provisional given the small, partly-unclear sample.

title: Condition of Premises at Delivery (Latent Defects, Hazardous Materials, Law Compliance)
where_to_look: The lease's defined-terms section for "Delivery Date"/"Commencement Date"; the "Premises" or "Condition of Premises" article (often near Article/Section 2); any standalone "Condition" representations-and-warranties section; and the indemnification article, specifically for carve-outs addressing pre-existing legal violations or hazardous materials.
required: Landlord must affirmatively warrant and deliver the Premises (i) broom-clean, (ii) in good order, condition, and repair, (iii) free of latent defects, (iv) in compliance with all applicable laws (including environmental laws), and (v) free of Hazardous Substances/materials — with an express Landlord obligation to cure any latent defect, law violation, or hazardous-material condition within a commercially reasonable time after notice. Layer on top of that baseline: (a) a rent-commencement delay/abatement remedy if Landlord misses the delivery date or delivers non-conforming Premises, (b) a Landlord representation and warranty that the Premises, common areas, and appurtenances comply with law and are free of hazardous material, and (c) a Landlord defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation for any pre-existing violation or hazardous material not caused by Tenant.
fallback: At minimum, secure the core delivery-condition standard plus the cure obligation: Landlord delivers broom-clean, in good order/condition/repair, free of latent defects, law-compliant, and free of Hazardous Substances, and must cure any such defect/violation/hazmat issue within a commercially reasonable time after written notice. This core package was obtained in every instance observed; the additional layers (rent-abatement remedy, standalone R&W section, full indemnification) were obtained in some but not all of the underlying deals and can be traded away first if Landlord resists.
escalate_if: Escalate regardless of how negotiations are trending if: Landlord insists on delivering the Premises strictly "AS-IS, WHERE-IS" with no condition standard, no cure obligation, and no exception for latent defects, law violations, or hazardous materials; Landlord discloses (or Tenant's due diligence uncovers) known or suspected pre-existing environmental contamination or an existing code/legal-compliance violation and Landlord refuses any indemnity or cure commitment for it; or the space is intended for industrial/manufacturing use (elevated hazmat exposure) and Landlord will not warrant freedom from Hazardous Substances at delivery.
flag_if: Lease has no defined delivery-condition standard, or defines delivery only as "AS-IS"/"WHERE-IS" with no carve-outs
No Landlord cure obligation (or no notice-and-cure period) for latent defects, law violations, or hazardous materials discovered after delivery
No remedy (e.g., rent-commencement delay/abatement) if Landlord fails to deliver on time or in the required condition
No Landlord indemnification for pre-existing environmental contamination or legal-compliance violations not caused by Tenant
No Landlord representation/warranty of law-compliance or freedom from hazardous material, or the representation is limited to the leased space only and excludes common areas/appurtenances
"Latent defect" or "Hazardous Substances/materials" is undefined or defined so narrowly it excludes likely real-world conditions
preferred_language: Condition of Premises at Delivery. Landlord shall deliver the Premises to Tenant on or before the Delivery Date in the following condition: (a) broom-clean; (b) in good order, condition, and repair; (c) free of latent defects; (d) in compliance with all applicable laws, ordinances, codes, and regulations, including without limitation all applicable environmental laws; and (e) free of any Hazardous Substances, except as expressly disclosed in Exhibit __. If, after the Delivery Date, any latent defect, violation of law, or presence of Hazardous Substances existing as of, or attributable to a condition first arising before, the Delivery Date is discovered, and such condition was not caused by Tenant or its agents, employees, or contractors, Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense, remedy such condition within a commercially reasonable time (not to exceed thirty (30) days after Landlord's receipt of written notice from Tenant, or such longer period as is reasonably necessary provided Landlord commences the cure within such thirty (30)-day period and thereafter diligently pursues completion). If Landlord fails to deliver the Premises in the condition required by this Section on or before the Delivery Date, the Rent Commencement Date shall be delayed one (1) day for each day of such delay or non-conformance. Landlord represents and warrants to Tenant that, as of the Delivery Date, the Premises, the Building, and all common areas and appurtenances thereto comply with all applicable laws, including environmental laws, and are free of Hazardous Substances. Landlord shall defend, indemnify, and hold Tenant harmless from and against any and all claims, damages, fines, penalties, and costs (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of any violation of law or the presence of Hazardous Substances at the Premises existing prior to, or not caused by Tenant after, the Delivery Date.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings from 2 distinct counterparty negotiations (Indiana Athletic Apparel, LLC — 1 finding; Providence Properties — 2 related findings from the same lease negotiation), all rated high significance and all pointing the same direction (silence/no standard → affirmative delivery-condition, cure, and remedy obligations on Landlord); treat this as a consistent but thin evidence base — effectively 2 independent deals — and revisit if additional findings surface a different pattern.
matching_clause_names: Delivery of Premises (Section 1.01 "Delivery Date" definition and new Section 2.01)

title: AS-IS Acceptance Carve-Outs Preserving Landlord's Ongoing Obligations
where_to_look: The "Condition of Premises" section (typically near the front of the lease, e.g., a Section 2.0x delivery-condition provision), the Tenant Improvements section and any related exhibit/allowance schedule, and — critically — any renewal or extension amendment's acceptance-of-premises language, since AS-IS disclaimers are frequently re-inserted or broadened at renewal.
required: An AS-IS/WHERE-IS acceptance clause (whether in the original lease, a Tenant Improvement/allowance provision, or a renewal/extension amendment) must be expressly made subject to, and must not be construed to waive, release, or override, any of Landlord's other obligations under the Lease as a whole — including delivery-condition obligations, and ongoing maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations — and, where the acceptance language appears in an amendment or extension, it must equally preserve Landlord's obligations under the Existing Lease being amended or extended, not just obligations stated within the amendment itself.
fallback: If Landlord resists a broad "subject to the Lease generally" carve-out, accept a narrower carve-out limited to obligations "expressly set forth" in the Lease (or Existing Lease, for renewals/amendments) — i.e., Landlord's disclaimer of improvement/repair obligations and Tenant's AS-IS acceptance do not override Landlord's existing maintenance, repair, and/or replacement obligations that are explicitly stated elsewhere in the governing lease document(s), even though implied or general obligations are not separately preserved.
escalate_if: Landlord's counsel proposes (or the base paper contains) a blanket AS-IS/WHERE-IS acceptance with NO carve-out at all — i.e., language stating Landlord has "no obligation whatsoever" to improve, maintain, or repair, with no reference back to obligations under the Lease or Existing Lease, and no exception preserving pre-existing maintenance/repair/replacement duties. This is the worst pre-negotiation position observed and should never be accepted as final; it must go to an attorney for a required carve-out to be negotiated back in, particularly for renewal/extension amendments where silence could be read as extinguishing Landlord's original-lease obligations.
flag_if: AS-IS/WHERE-IS acceptance language with no cross-reference to "this Lease," "the Existing Lease," or Landlord's other obligations — i.e., the disclaimer stands alone or only references a narrow exhibit

A renewal or extension amendment where Tenant re-accepts the Premises AS-IS for the new term but the carve-out (if any) is limited to obligations stated "herein"/"in this Amendment" rather than also covering the Existing Lease

A Tenant Improvement or allowance provision disclaiming Landlord's obligation "to improve the Premises, Building, or Common Areas" without an exception for Landlord's existing maintenance/repair/replacement obligations

Absence of a phrase resembling "except as otherwise expressly provided in this Lease" or "subject to Landlord's obligations under the Existing Lease" adjacent to any AS-IS or no-obligation-to-improve language
Broad disclaimers of representations and warranties bundled together with (and potentially bleeding into a waiver of) Landlord's ongoing repair/maintenance covenants elsewhere in the lease
preferred_language: Tenant's acceptance of the Premises (including, if applicable, the Premises during any Extension or Renewal Term) in its "AS-IS, WHERE-IS" condition, without representation or warranty of any kind by Landlord, shall not release, diminish, waive, or otherwise be construed to override any obligation of Landlord under this Lease (or, if this instrument amends or extends an existing lease, under such existing lease, the "Existing Lease"), including without limitation any obligation relating to the delivery condition of the Premises and any obligation to maintain, repair, or replace the Premises, the Building, and/or the Common Areas. Nothing in this Section, in any Tenant Improvement or allowance provision of this Lease, or in Landlord's disclaimer of any obligation to improve the Premises, Building, or Common Areas, shall be interpreted to excuse Landlord from performing any obligation otherwise imposed on Landlord under this Lease or the Existing Lease, and all such obligations shall survive and remain in full force and effect notwithstanding Tenant's AS-IS acceptance of the Premises. [Fallback, if the above is rejected: substitute "any obligation expressly set forth in this Lease (or the Existing Lease, as applicable)" for "any obligation ... under this Lease."]
confidence_note: Based on only 3 findings drawn from 2 distinct counterparties (2 of the 3 findings come from the same lease-extension negotiation/amendment), so this is a thin sample; however, the direction was fully consistent across all three — every negotiated outcome broadened or added a carve-out preserving Landlord's pre-existing/ongoing obligations against an AS-IS or no-improvement-obligation disclaimer — which is why this is set at PRESS rather than MUST PRESS or MANAGE; treat the specific fallback/escalation thresholds as provisional pending more data points.

title: Tenant Improvements: Scope, Discretion & Landlord Approval
where_to_look: The lease's "Tenant Improvements" / "Alterations" section (commonly its own numbered section, e.g. Section 7, or a Work Letter/Exhibit); the "Condition of Premises" or delivery-condition clause; any Tenant Improvement Allowance provisions in the Basic Lease Information page or an improvements exhibit; and the sub-clause governing Landlord's review/approval of Tenant's construction drawings or plans.
required: (1) The lease should state Landlord's delivery condition and the cost allocation for any improvements beyond that condition explicitly and specifically — not a bare "as-is" — ideally including a Landlord-funded Tenant Improvement Allowance for base-building items. (2) Tenant should have express language confirming that the decision to make improvements "necessary or desirable" for its business operations rests in Tenant's sole discretion, subject only to Landlord's approval as separately provided. (3) Landlord's approval of Tenant's construction drawings/plans must be expressly subject to a "not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" standard, ideally paired with a deemed-approval mechanism (e.g., approval deemed given if Landlord does not respond with reasonably specific objections within 10 business days).
fallback: Where the full package above isn't obtainable, secure at minimum: (a) the "necessary or desirable" scope language plus the express statement that the decision whether to improve is Tenant's, "subject to Landlord approval as set forth herein"; and (b) an express "not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" qualifier on Landlord's approval of construction drawings, even without a deemed-approval clock. Cost allocation can be accepted on an as-is-plus-limited-landlord-obligation basis (e.g., Landlord paints/preps only, Tenant funds the rest) provided the scope of Landlord's limited obligation and the resulting Tenant cost responsibility are stated with specificity rather than left to inference — this is the pattern actually observed in the negotiated outcomes reviewed.
escalate_if: Escalate to an attorney regardless of how negotiations are otherwise going if: (a) Landlord's approval of Tenant's TI plans is left entirely to Landlord's "sole" or "absolute" discretion with no reasonableness qualifier whatsoever; (b) Landlord's consent right extends beyond approving construction drawings to approving the underlying business decision to improve (i.e., Landlord can veto whether Tenant improves the space, not just how); or (c) the premises delivery condition is undefined or purely "as-is" while Landlord simultaneously retains broad, unqualified approval rights over any improvements Tenant would need just to make the space usable — that combination can leave Tenant unable to both fund and obtain approval for improvements it needs to operate.
flag_if: Construction-drawing/plan approval clause requires Landlord's consent with no "reasonable," "not unreasonably withheld," or similar qualifying standard attached
Improvement-scope language is limited to "necessary" (omitting "or desirable") and/or does not expressly confirm the decision to improve rests with Tenant

"Condition of Premises" is defined only as "as-is" with Landlord's stated obligations limited to cosmetic/minor items (e.g., painting) and no Tenant Improvement Allowance or clear delineation of who funds the rest
No stated response deadline or deemed-approval mechanism for Landlord's review of TI plans, leaving approval timing entirely open-ended
Approval standard uses "sole discretion" or "absolute discretion" language specifically tied to TI plan approval rather than to unrelated lease matters
preferred_language: Tenant Improvements; Landlord Approval. Tenant shall have the right, at its sole cost and expense (except to the extent of any Landlord contribution expressly set forth in this Lease), to construct in the Premises such improvements, alterations, and installations as Tenant deems necessary or desirable for its business operations (the "Tenant Improvements"), and Tenant's decision whether to undertake any Tenant Improvements shall be in Tenant's sole discretion. Prior to commencing any Tenant Improvements requiring Landlord's consent under this Lease, Tenant shall submit construction drawings and plans to Landlord for approval, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. If Landlord fails to approve or disapprove such plans (stating with reasonable specificity the grounds for any disapproval) within ten (10) business days after receipt of a complete submission, such plans shall be deemed approved. Landlord's condition of delivery of the Premises, and the allocation of costs for any improvements beyond that condition — including any Tenant Improvement Allowance to be funded by Landlord — shall be expressly and specifically set forth in this Lease, and the Premises shall not be delivered on a bare "as-is" basis without such express allocation.
confidence_note: Based on only 3 findings, and effectively 2 distinct counterparty negotiations (2 of the 3 findings — the discretion-scope and approval-standard changes — come from the same lease with the same landlord); all three are rated "medium" significance, not "high." The direction is internally consistent (broader tenant discretion, explicit reasonableness standard on approval, more specific cost/condition allocation), but the sample is too thin to call this a firmly established market pattern — treat this rule as provisional and revisit once more findings on this topic are available.

title: Repairs & Maintenance Allocation / Building Systems Upkeep
where_to_look: The "Repairs and Maintenance" (or "Maintenance and Repairs") section of the lease body; any rider/addendum addressing fire protection, sprinkler, PIV (post indicator valve), or other life-safety/building-systems testing; and HVAC/mechanical or "Building Systems" provisions. Also check the original term sheet/LOI — a bare one-line "Tenant is responsible for all maintenance" term-sheet statement is a common starting point that gets substantially rebuilt in the actual lease.
required: Landlord bears responsibility for maintaining, repairing, and replacing all structural and major building-system components — foundation, roof, exterior walls/structure, exterior and subterranean utility lines (water, gas, sewer, electrical) up to their point of entry into the Premises, any HVAC system not serving the Premises exclusively, and the sprinkler/fire-protection system. Landlord must also affirmatively maintain and test life-safety systems on a defined schedule (monthly PIV exercise; quarterly fire-protection/sprinkler testing), keep written records of that testing, and make those records available to Tenant on request. Tenant's obligation is limited to routine, non-structural, interior maintenance of the Premises and equipment serving it exclusively.
fallback: If Landlord resists the full allocation, fall back to securing Landlord responsibility for at minimum the "big four" structural items (roof, foundation, exterior walls, base-building/shared HVAC) plus the fire-protection/sprinkler system itself, even if the formal testing-and-recordkeeping schedule (monthly PIV, quarterly system test, written records on request) is negotiated down to a general "Landlord shall comply with applicable fire code and insurance testing requirements" obligation rather than the specific procedure. Do not fall back below Landlord owning the structural shell and life-safety system itself — only the documentation/frequency detail is a reasonable trade.
escalate_if: Escalate to an attorney and do not accept if: (1) the lease assigns Tenant sole and undifferentiated responsibility for "all maintenance of the Premises" with no landlord carve-out for structural components, roof, or shared/base-building systems; (2) the lease is silent on landlord testing/maintenance of fire protection, sprinkler, or PIV systems and instead disclaims landlord liability for their condition or failure; or (3) Tenant would be required to indemnify Landlord for injury, property damage, or business interruption arising from a structural failure or an untested/unmaintained life-safety system that was never Tenant's to inspect or control.
flag_if: Maintenance clause is a single undifferentiated sentence (e.g., 'Tenant shall maintain the Premises') with no express landlord carve-out for structural or major-system items
No allocation at all for roof, foundation, or exterior wall/structural maintenance
HVAC, plumbing, or electrical equipment serving other tenants or common/base-building areas is assigned to Tenant rather than Landlord
Lease or addenda contain no fire protection / sprinkler / PIV testing obligation on Landlord, or the topic is entirely absent
No requirement for Landlord to create or share written records of life-safety system testing
Subterranean or exterior utility lines are made Tenant's responsibility beyond the point of entry into the Premises
The operative 'Repairs and Maintenance' language still reads like unedited term-sheet boilerplate (one line, no landlord/tenant split) rather than a fully built-out multi-part clause
preferred_language:
Repairs and Maintenance.
(a) By Tenant. Except as expressly set forth in this Section, Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, keep and maintain the interior, non-structural portions of the Premises in good order, condition, and repair, including routine maintenance of interior fixtures, finishes, and any equipment serving the Premises exclusively, reasonable wear and tear and casualty excepted.
(b) By Landlord. Landlord shall maintain, repair, and replace, as and when needed, and keep in good working order: (i) the foundation and structural elements of the building; (ii) the roof, including the roof membrane and structural roof deck; (iii) the exterior walls and structural components of the Premises; (iv) the exterior and subterranean portions of the water, gas, sewer, and plumbing lines and electrical facilities, up to their point of entry into the Premises; (v) any heating, ventilating, and air conditioning system that does not serve the Premises exclusively; and (vi) the sprinkler system and other fire protection or life-safety systems serving the building, if any.
(c) Fire Protection and Life-Safety Systems Testing. Landlord shall (i) physically exercise all post indicator valves (PIVs) located on the exterior of the facility on a monthly basis, which testing shall include, without limitation, confirming that each valve is open, closing the valve three full turns, and reopening the valve; and (ii) test all fire protection systems, no less than quarterly, including all water-flow alarms and sprinkler control valve tampers. Landlord shall maintain written records of the foregoing testing and shall make such records available for review by Tenant, or Tenant's employees, agents, or designees, upon request.
confidence_note: Based on only 2 findings (from 2 different counterparties/deals — one general lease repairs-and-maintenance clause, one fire-protection/PIV testing addendum), both rated high significance and both showing the same direction of movement (Landlord taking on structural/major-system upkeep and documented life-safety testing that was absent or Tenant-only in the starting position); the sample is thin, so treat this rule as directionally consistent but still provisional pending more data points.

title: Fitting-Out Period / Rent-Free Period & Fit-Out Logistics
where_to_look: The Definitions clause (where "Fitting-Out Period" and "Rent Free Period" are defined, e.g. Clause 2.1), and the substantive "Availability of Demised Premises for Fitting-Out Works" / "Possession and Tenant's Fitting-Out Works" clause (often Clause 7 or similar) together with any First/Second Schedule specifying fit-out conditions and landlord-provided fixtures.
required: A defined Fitting-Out Period of adequate length, commencing on the later of lease execution or actual delivery of possession, during which no rent, service charge, or other outgoings accrue; free pre-period access for measuring/planning; landlord approval of fit-out plans on a "not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" standard with a defined response/deemed-approval window; a day-for-day extension of the Fitting-Out Period for any landlord delay in delivering possession; and a qualified (not blanket) waiver of tenant claims for landlord's own concurrent building works, carved out for landlord's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
fallback: A defined Fitting-Out Period with specific start/end dates and a coextensive Rent-Free Period (rent and service charges suspended for the full fit-out window); tenant given reasonable pre-period access solely for drawings/plans; landlord retains approval rights over fit-out plans (not unreasonably withheld) and requires prior lease execution as a condition of access; tenant bears its own fit-out costs and is restricted to 8:00am-midnight work hours without disturbing other tenants; landlord keeps an essentially unqualified right to carry out its own works during the period with tenant waiving claims arising from that work; and landlord's fixture/fitting obligation is capped to what is listed in the schedule, with no tenant right to demand more.
escalate_if: The lease leaves "Fitting-Out Period" / "Rent Free Period" as "Not Applicable," blank, or otherwise undefined, with rent accruing from execution/commencement regardless of the tenant's ability to occupy and fit out (this was the actual starting position in every sampled instance and must never be accepted as a final position); the landlord's own-works exculpation is broadened to cover the full Term (not just the Fitting-Out Period) or to waive claims for landlord's willful misconduct/gross negligence; there is no outside date for delivery of possession or no reasonableness/timing standard on the landlord's plan-approval right; or the Fitting-Out Period/Rent-Free Period dates are left blank at signature.
flag_if: Definitions clause shows "Fitting-Out Period" or "Rent Free Period" marked "Not Applicable," blank, or omitted entirely
No clause obligating the landlord to make the premises available for fit-out prior to rent commencement
Tenant's waiver of claims for landlord's concurrent building works is unqualified (no carve-out for negligence/willful misconduct) or extends beyond the Fitting-Out Period
Approval of tenant's fit-out plans has no "not unreasonably withheld" standard or response-time/deemed-approval mechanism
No day-for-day extension of the Fitting-Out Period when the landlord delays delivering possession
Landlord's fixture/fitting delivery obligation is vague or not tied to a specific schedule/exhibit
Fit-out work-hour restrictions or access conditions are narrow enough to make the fit-out period practically unusable (e.g., no access outside a tight daily window, no weekend/holiday access)
preferred_language:
7.1 Fitting-Out Period. Landlord shall make the Premises available to Tenant for Tenant's fit-out works for a period of [__] days (the "Fitting-Out Period"), commencing on the later of (a) the date of execution of this Lease and (b) the date Landlord delivers possession of the Premises to Tenant in the condition required under Schedule [__]. No Base Rent, service charge, or other Additional Rent shall accrue or be payable during the Fitting-Out Period. If Landlord fails to deliver possession of the Premises in the required condition by the scheduled delivery date, the Fitting-Out Period shall be extended day-for-day for each day of delay.

7.2 Pre-Access for Planning. Prior to the commencement of the Fitting-Out Period, Landlord shall grant Tenant and its designers/contractors reasonable access to the Premises, at reasonable hours and at no cost or rent liability, solely for the purpose of measuring, inspecting, and preparing fit-out drawings and plans.

7.3 Approval of Plans. Tenant shall submit its proposed fit-out plans to Landlord for approval, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Landlord shall respond within [10] business days of submission; failure to respond within such period shall be deemed approval.

7.4 Tenant's Fit-Out Works. Tenant shall perform its fit-out works at its own cost and expense, in accordance with the approved plans and applicable law. Tenant may perform such works between 8:00 a.m. and midnight, provided Tenant does not unreasonably disturb other occupants of the building. Any delay in completion of Tenant's fit-out works, other than delay caused by Landlord, shall not extend the Fitting-Out Period or excuse Tenant's other obligations under this Lease.

7.5 Landlord's Concurrent Works. If Landlord carries out its own works in the Premises or the building during the Fitting-Out Period, Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize interference with Tenant's fit-out works. Tenant waives claims against Landlord for costs, damages, or delay arising from such Landlord works performed in compliance with applicable law or regulatory requirement, except to the extent caused by Landlord's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

7.6 Landlord's Fixtures. Landlord shall deliver the Premises with the fixtures and fittings described in Schedule [__] ("Landlord's Fixtures") in good working condition as of the commencement of the Fitting-Out Period. Tenant shall have no claim to any fixtures or fittings beyond those specified in Schedule [__].

[Drafting note: this is a first-draft implementation of the REQUIRED position only, not reviewed by counsel; conform defined terms (Premises, Term, Base Rent, etc.) to the governing lease's existing definitions.]
confidence_note: Based on only 3 findings, and all 3 trace back to the same counterparty (Royal & Sons Investments Pte Ltd) across what appear to be two related lease negotiations, not three independent deals -- the directional pattern (landlord's base template offers no fit-out/rent-free period at all; Marmon's tenant side adds a dated, rent-free Fitting-Out Period while accepting the landlord's own-works exculpation and a fixture cap) is internally consistent, but the evidence is narrow and single-counterparty, so treat elements of "required" that go beyond what was actually observed in the "after" text (e.g., the qualified exculpation carve-out, deemed-approval timing, day-for-day extension) as aspirational drafting rather than a proven negotiated outcome, and prioritize this as PRESS rather than MUST PRESS pending more diverse samples.
